title: Redwood + StellarNet Joint Solution Techsync
summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for a joint solution (AuroraCloud + Redwood inference), and next steps for a technical preview. Discussed listing metadata, terraform/helm artifacts, security controls (SSO, KMS), and a pilot benchmark plan.
topics: security/compliance: SSO, KMS, audit logs, data residency
next_steps: Redwood (Anil) to share initial reference architecture diagram and terraform snippets by 2026-12-09
StellarNet to provide a sandbox account and sample workload by 2026-12-10
Sarah to send marketplace listing checklist and preferred image assets list by 2026-12-04
Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2026-12-14
action_items: Anil Patel (Redwood SE): Create reference arch diagram + helm/terraform snippets (due 2026-12-09)
Sarah Cole (Redwood AE): Send marketplace metadata checklist and pricing guidance (due 2026-12-04)
Emma Li (StellarNet): Share sandbox account details and sample dataset (due 2026-12-10)
Tom Baker (StellarNet PM): Confirm marketing assets and joint solution description for listing (due 2026-12-11)
transcript:
[00:00] Sarah Cole: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to run through the joint solution techsync for Redwood and Stellarnet. quick intros?
[00:10] Emma Li: Hi I'm Emma, head of cloud at Stellarnet, thanks for setting this up.
[00:15] Rajesh Kumar: Rajesh, platform eng, I'll be hands on.
[00:20] Tom Baker: Tom, partner PM, I'll handle marketplace bits.
[00:26] Sarah Cole: Great, Anil from my team is the SE, he'll walk the reference arch and the technical artifacts we wanted to sync on.
[00:33] Anil Patel: Hey all, thanks. so high level I want to align on three things: the marketplace listing packaging, the reference architecture (networking/VPC/KMS flows), and the pilot/benchmark plan.
[00:45] Rajesh Kumar: Sounds good. on marketplace, we need to know what artifacts you require — images, terraform modules, helm charts, pricing metadata, legal blurb, that sort of thing.
[00:55] Sarah Cole: Yep. we'll share a checklist but core items are: listing description, one architecture diagram, terraform example for provisioning Redwood connectors and any required infra on your side, container images or AMI references for any partner-provided components, and screenshots or marketing assets.
[01:12] Tom Baker: For the screenshot / assets part, do you need them in a specific size or format?
[01:16] Sarah Cole: Preferred sizes are in the checklist, png and high res jpeg for marketing, and a 1024x512 hero image. we can accept svg for diagrams.
[01:25] Anil Patel: On the reference arch, key items to capture: where the customer data lives, how requests flow to Redwood hosted or dedicated endpoints, and how keys are managed. For Stellarnet joint solution we discussed AuroraCloud hosting model — we assume customers will use your managed vpc peering to Redwood private endpoints, or they'll use the marketplace flow where the listing provisions connectors into their account.
[01:47] Emma Li: Correct, we prefer the listing to support both patterns; many of our customers require VPC private endpoints and KMS integration.
[01:54] Rajesh Kumar: For KMS we use our HSM-backed KMS, will Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[02:00] Anil Patel: Yes, Redwood private supports customer KMS (we call it bring-your-own-KMS), and we can show the flow in the diagram. we should note any extra steps for dedicated vs hosted. sometimes the docs call it BYO-KMS or BYOK.
[02:14] Sarah Cole: Also SOC 2 and audit log requirements — we will attach our compliance pack but we need Stellarnet to confirm any additional compliance statements for the listing.
[02:23] Tom Baker: We'll pull our compliance notes and provide a statement.
[02:26] Rajesh Kumar: On packaging, what's the expectation for terraform vs helm?
[02:30] Anil Patel: Terraform example to provision the reversible connector and RBAC, plus a helm chart for deploying any sidecar or adapter that sits in your account. terraform should be fairly minimal — provider config, module invocation, example variables.
[02:43] Emma Li: Will you accept a quickstart repo? our customers like one-click deploy.
[02:47] Sarah Cole: Yes, a quickstart repo is excellent. we can include a marketplace listing that links to the quickstart. Also, we prefer sample architecture diagrams in the repo and a short README with the expected traffic patterns and recommended instance types.
[03:00] Anil Patel: About traffic patterns — we should document token rates, typical concurrency and KV cache behavior. For RLHF style workloads the memory/KV cache sizes matter. can you share typical workloads?
[03:13] Rajesh Kumar: We have a sample user-query workload (conversational customer support), about 50 qps per tenant at peak, average prompt length 120 tokens, responses 80 tokens.
[03:24] Anil Patel: Perfect, that'll inform kernel selection and batching guidance. We'll recommend quantization and batching settings for cost targets.
[03:32] Tom Baker: On the marketplace billing side, is there a preferred model? flat fee + usage or purely usage?
[03:38] Sarah Cole: Redwood supports a couple of models; for marketplace we usually do a per-usage pass-through where the partner lists pricing and we surface it, or a subscription. Sarah continues: For this joint solution pilots customers usually start with usage-based during prototyping.
[03:53] Emma Li: Ok. security — SSO and SAML? our customers want SSO into the management console and single-tenant RBAC.
[04:00] Anil Patel: Redwood supports SAML/SSO and SSO provisioning via SCIM, RBAC at token and route level. We'll include SSO/SCIM integration notes in the reference arch doc.
[04:11] Rajesh Kumar: Audit logs and retention — how much detail do you capture?
[04:16] Anil Patel: We capture request-level metadata, token-level cost attribution and an audit trail for administrative actions. Retention policies are configurable; enterprise customers often ask for 12 months retention. We'll note default retention and options.
[04:31] Sarah Cole: One common gotcha: data residency. If a customer needs EU-only, we need to note region pinning in the listing and reference arch.
[04:39] Emma Li: Good point. many of our EU customers require region pinning and dedicated tenancy.
[04:44] Anil Patel: We'll show the routing policy options — region, cost, latency, and fallback. For the pilot let's pick one region and run benchmarks there.
[04:53] Tom Baker: Benchmark plan — what do you need from us to run a quick pilot?
[04:57] Anil Patel: We'll need a sandbox account, sample dataset, and expected SLAs. We'll run a scripted load with your sample workload, collect latency/throughput/cost metrics, and share a benchmark spreadsheet.
[05:10] Rajesh Kumar: Timing?
[05:12] Anil Patel: If we get assets this week, we can run the pilot next week and share results within 7 days.
[05:18] Sarah Cole: I'll coordinate availability.
[05:20] Emma Li: One question about the listing copy: can Redwood edit the blurb or do you need final approval?
[05:26] Tom Baker: we prefer Redwood to draft and we'll approve.
[05:29] Sarah Cole: That's fine. we'll draft the marketplace listing and loop you for approval.
[05:34] Rajesh Kumar: Any special networking like peering vs private link?
[05:38] Anil Patel: Both are options; we recommend private endpoints (PrivateLink) for minimal public surface. We'll show both flows in the arch. note that private endpoints require some partner infra changes — we'll capture them in the terraform example.
[05:52] Emma Li: For the helm chart, do you want us to own the adapter image or will Redwood provide?
[05:57] Anil Patel: Either works. if you provide the adapter we ask for a container image repo and build instructions. if we provide one, we'll coordinate on image signing.
[06:07] Tom Baker: Signing — we need images signed for our enterprise customers.
[06:10] Anil Patel: We support OCI image signing; we'll include a guide.
[06:15] Sarah Cole: Ok let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[06:19] Anil Patel: Recap: Redwood to share reference arch + terraform + helm snippets; StellarNet to share sandbox and assets; Redwood to draft listing copy; agree pilot dates.
[06:29] Emma Li: That works.
[06:31] Sarah Cole: Anything else?
[06:33] Tom Baker: One small ask — can we get a short video walkthrough of the quickstart for the marketplace page?
[06:38] Sarah Cole: Yes we can record a 3-5 minute walkthrough. I'll include that in the checklist.
[06:44] Rajesh Kumar: Great.
[06:46] Sarah Cole: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts.
[06:50] Emma Li: Thanks, talk soon.
[06:53] [call ends]
notes: Shared items: marketplace checklist (will be sent by Sarah), reference arch draft (Anil)
Pilot: 1 region, sample workload (50 qps, 120/80 token split), timeline target week of 2026-12-14
Compliance: Redwood to attach SOC2/ISO docs; Stellarnet to provide any additional compliance statements
